newsitem.title: FINLAND: Privatisation to boost Finland R&D spending - govt.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation to boost Finland R&D spending - govt.

text.p: The Finnish government said on Friday it will raise public research and development spending, making it possible to raise total national R&D expenditure to 2.9 percent of GDP in 1999 from about 2.5 percent at present.
"Public R&D spending will gradually be increased during the years 1997-1999 so that in 1999 it will be about 7.5 billion markka," the government said in a statement.

The increase in public research and development spending "will be financed by revenues from the sale of certain state-owned companies", it said, adding prospects for broadening the ownership of state-controlled companies were good. @
"By increasing public R&D expenditure Finland ensures that by the end of the century Finland will be among the leading countries in terms of its GDP share of R&D expenditure," it said.
The statement gave no details of which state companies would be privatised.
"The equilibrium of the state finances will not be impaired by this decision," the government said.
It has earlier decided to allocate one billion markka per year of revenue from privatisation to controlling public debt.
The R&D policy agreed by the government's ministerial economic policy committee would further strengthen opportunities for economic growth and improved employment, it said.
Of total Finnish R&D spending, about 40 percent comes from public resources and about 60 percent from the private sector. @
"According to current assumptions expenditure within the private sector will remain high over the next few years," the government said.
Total R&D spending would be about 15.5 billion markka in 1997 and about 18 billion markka in 1999, it said.
